correctness.rationale: The two individually coloured anchors make both distance functions recoverable within d rounds. The next round counts neighbours decreasing both distances; precisely each common-anchor coordinate where x differs contributes one such neighbour, giving s, and r=b+s-h0 and t=b+s-h1. Explicit anchor-fixing graph automorphisms are transitive on each (s,r,t) class; hence the colour partition is exactly the orbit partition and stabilizes by d+1. All parameter boundaries q>=3,d>=1,1<=b<=d are addressed and class-size multinomials enumerate each orbit. checks/check_refinement.py and checks/check_local_statistic.py; reproducible reports 52 parameter configurations and 16043 vertices. Finite tests are corroborative, not the proof.

value.rationale: The result supplies a complete uniform orbit classification and exact cell-size/count data for two individually marked vertices in natural nonbinary Hamming graphs. A concrete H(3,3) obstruction demonstrates that two anchor-distance values alone do not determine the stable partition, while one local neighbour statistic does; this discriminates stabilizer orbit reconstruction from elementary landmark distances, and the theorem applies to every alphabet q>=3 and every dimension, not arbitrary ad hoc slices. No downstream or generic graph-identification benefit is presumed.
